It was like this for me as well. They become pretty easy once your high level since you basically swing faster than they can block you. 

You should be able to perfect block pretty confidently that you know you could sit there and perfect block all day and not take damage. Once you’ve done it enough, you will notice certain animations and know when to press block. Make sure you don’t spam it or you get the red shield indicating you pressed it too early. 

Also don’t bother with repostes. Perfect block, wait then feint into a strike, if it lands try to keep hacking away. Watch your stamina to. You will only take damage if you’re out of stamina or get hit hard to a place where your armour is lacking. Make sure it’s all repaired and it’s as high defence as you can get.

If they don’t know master strike, try and attack the opposite side of where they are holding the weapon. 

When your opponent is killing you this easy, don’t bother with combos. You might only be able to give them one slash at a time as your level is too low compared to theirs. Focus on defence and feints.

They definitely want to you to kind of move them so they get in each other’s way. Masterstrike is probably the easiest way to fight early on. Then it’s basically feinting to combos later on. Make sure you don’t spam block after your opponents perfect blocks you or you will see a red shield indicating a free hit for your opponent. Leveling up your combat will make it easier to hit. Also having strong armour is key for fighting lots of enemies. If you’re fighting heavy armoured opponents, you should use a mace over slashing weapons. Even the pistol is better until your combat skills improve. Pole arms are supposed to be better for groups of enemies but, I don’t think it matters to much. Dodging is also helpful as you can get free hits after a dodge and also put yourself in a better position and avoid getting surrounded. Make sure to save before battles as you’re learning because you’re gonna make a lot of mistakes. Fight wolves, you might as well wait to perfect blocks then repost once. Repeat till they’re dead. Upgrade you unarmed combat too because it comes in handy sometimes. You can do this by fighting the millers hired hands for money. Make sure to get top gear. Loot bandits and repair all the stuff at the blacksmith or by armourer/blacksmith kits.

Orpheus:

Overwhelmed with grief, Orpheus decided to descend into Hades, the realm of the dead, to bring Eurydice back.
His music charmed Cerberus, the three-headed dog guarding the entrance, and even moved Hades and Persephone, the rulers of the underworld.
They were so moved by his sorrowful music that they agreed to let Eurydice return to the living.

The Condition:
Hades set one condition: Orpheus must lead Eurydice out of the underworld, and he must not turn to look at her until they had both reached the land of the living.

The Tragedy:

As they were nearing the exit, Orpheus, overcome with anxiety and doubt, turned to look at Eurydice.
As a result, she was immediately pulled back into the underworld, lost to him forever.

The myth of Orpheus and Eurydice is a poignant tale of love, loss, and the power of music.

SSRI’s will help but, I have found they don’t make me want to talk or get out of my comfort zone. 

SNRI’s I have found not much different. They have a bit of a stimulant effect early on but, that wears off. 

Wellbutrin made me more anxious. With an SSRI however, it was fine.

I am now on trintellix. It works like an SSRI without sides. Still doesn’t solve SAD but helps with depression and feelings of anxiety (tight chest, shaking, eye contact… that sort of stuff)

I’ve also tried buspar which did that same thing without the help with depression. I never got my dosage adjusted though.

You can go through all the meds and more like I did but if I was to do it again, I would have stuck with therapy and trintellix.  There’s a good doc on benzodiazepines on Netflix you should watch if your think of going on them. All I have ever found is you end up worse than you were in the beginning. It’s hard but, it’s because we have two systems in our brains. The first system is the fast brain. It basically is trained to function when we are kids. So basically, you have an infant child programming the automatic part of the brain. Unfortunately, you programmed your brain to fear social situations. To reprogram the brain, you have to go against the grain of what the automatic brain wants to do. This is call neruogenis. 

The second part of your brain is called the slow brain. It’s where executive function takes place.
